iceland/blue-lagoon.name: Blue Lagoon
iceland/blue-lagoon.description: A milky-blue geothermal pool in a black lava field near the airport, a popular first or last stop for the trip.
iceland/blue-lagoon.details: The Blue Lagoon is a man-made lagoon fed by the outflow of a nearby geothermal power plant, with silica-rich water that stays warm even in winter. It lies about twenty minutes from Keflavik Airport and is a popular way to start or end a trip. Entry is by timed ticket, so booking ahead is essential, and a shower before entering is compulsory. Volcanic activity on the Reykjanes peninsula has caused temporary closures in recent years, so check its current status before building a plan around it.

iceland/hallgrimskirkja.name: Hallgrímskirkja
iceland/hallgrimskirkja.description: Reykjavik's tall concrete church, shaped like basalt columns, with a tower lift to a view over the colourful rooftops.
iceland/hallgrimskirkja.details: Hallgrímskirkja was designed by the architect Guðjón Samúelsson and its stepped, columnar form recalls the basalt formations found around Iceland. Construction began in 1945 and took more than forty years. A lift runs up the tower to an observation deck with views across the city, harbour and mountains. The church is an active place of worship, so the tower may close during services, and a statue of Leif Erikson stands outside.

iceland/harpa-seafront.name: Harpa and the Reykjavik seafront
iceland/harpa-seafront.description: A glass-fronted concert hall on the harbour and a sculpture of a steel ship, linked by a walk along the shore.
iceland/harpa-seafront.details: Harpa opened in 2011 and is known for its honeycomb glass facade, designed with the artist Ólafur Eliasson, which shifts in colour with the light. The Sun Voyager, a steel sculpture of a boat frame by the shore, is a short walk away and faces the sea and mountains across the bay. The seafront path is flat and pleasant for an evening stroll, and the wind off the water can be strong and cold even in summer.

iceland/reykjavik-whale-watching.name: Whale-watching from Reykjavik
iceland/reykjavik-whale-watching.description: A boat trip from the Old Harbour into Faxaflói bay to look for minke whales, humpbacks, dolphins and seabirds.
iceland/reykjavik-whale-watching.details: Boats leave from the Old Harbour on trips lasting around three hours into Faxaflói bay, where minke whales, white-beaked dolphins and, in summer, humpback whales are regularly seen. Sightings are never guaranteed, and many operators offer another trip free if nothing is seen. Warm outer layers are provided by most boats because it is cold on the water even in summer. People prone to seasickness should take precautions, as the bay can be rough.

iceland/reykjavik-dinner.name: Icelandic dinner in Reykjavik
iceland/reykjavik-dinner.description: A meal of local lamb, fresh fish and fish stew in a downtown restaurant.
iceland/reykjavik-dinner.details: Iceland's restaurant scene draws on very fresh fish, free-range lamb and dairy, and traditional dishes such as fish stew, grilled lamb and skyr desserts are standard menu items. Most places have English menus and are used to visitors. Booking ahead is wise at weekends and in summer. Restaurants are generally more expensive than in mainland Europe, so many visitors balance them with simpler meals.

iceland/thingvellir.name: Thingvellir National Park
iceland/thingvellir.description: A rift valley where the North American and Eurasian plates are pulling apart, and the site of Iceland's medieval parliament.
iceland/thingvellir.details: Thingvellir is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the place where the Icelandic parliament, the Althing, first met in 930. The park lies in a rift valley between two tectonic plates, which can be seen as cliffs and fissures running through the lava plain, and a path leads along the base of the main rift wall. A clear-watered lake lies beside it. The paths are flat or gently sloped, and in winter they can be icy.

iceland/geysir.name: Geysir geothermal area
iceland/geysir.description: A field of hot springs and fumaroles where the Strokkur geyser erupts every few minutes.
iceland/geysir.details: The Geysir area gave its name to all geysers, though the original Great Geysir erupts rarely now. Its neighbour Strokkur shoots a column of water some twenty metres into the air every five to ten minutes, which makes it easy to watch. The ground is hot and scalding, so keep to the marked paths and barriers. A smell of sulphur hangs over the area, and the site is free to enter.

iceland/gullfoss.name: Gullfoss
iceland/gullfoss.description: The Golden Falls, a two-tier waterfall on the Hvítá river dropping into a narrow canyon.
iceland/gullfoss.details: Gullfoss is one of Iceland's best-known waterfalls, where the Hvítá river drops in two steps before plunging into a deep canyon. Paths lead to viewpoints at different levels, including one close to the upper falls where the spray soaks visitors. In winter, ice makes the paths slippery and parts may be closed. Waterproofs are worth carrying all year.

iceland/seljalandsfoss.name: Seljalandsfoss
iceland/seljalandsfoss.description: A tall waterfall on the south coast that visitors can walk behind on a path in the cliff.
iceland/seljalandsfoss.details: Seljalandsfoss drops about sixty metres from a cliff above the coastal plain, and a path allows walkers to go behind the falling water. The path is wet and slippery, and is closed in icy conditions, so waterproofs and shoes with grip are needed. A short walk along the cliff leads to Gljúfrabúi, a smaller waterfall hidden in a narrow canyon. It is right beside the Ring Road and very easy to reach.

iceland/skogafoss.name: Skógafoss
iceland/skogafoss.description: A broad sixty-metre waterfall with a staircase up to a viewing platform at the top.
iceland/skogafoss.details: Skógafoss is a wide curtain of water falling about sixty metres over an old sea cliff, and often shows a rainbow on sunny days. A staircase on the side climbs to a platform above the falls, from where the Fimmvörðuháls hiking trail continues up the river. It is a short walk from the car park. Spray can drench the area at the base, and the steps are slippery in winter.

iceland/dyrholaey.name: Dyrhólaey
iceland/dyrholaey.description: A high headland with a sea arch and lighthouse, and a good place to see puffins in summer.
iceland/dyrholaey.details: Dyrhólaey is a promontory over the south coast with a large rock arch and a lighthouse on top, giving views along the black sand beaches in both directions. Puffins nest on the cliffs in summer. Parts of the area are closed in the early nesting season, usually from mid-May to late June, to protect the birds. The top is reached by a rough road and is very windy.

iceland/reynisfjara.name: Reynisfjara black sand beach
iceland/reynisfjara.description: A beach of black volcanic sand with basalt columns and rock stacks standing in the surf near Vík.
iceland/reynisfjara.details: Reynisfjara is known for its black sand, a cave framed by basalt columns and the Reynisdrangar sea stacks offshore. It is also dangerous: unpredictable waves, known as sneaker waves, surge far up the beach without warning and have killed visitors. Keep well back from the water, never turn your back on the sea and heed the warning signs. Even so, it is one of the most striking places on the south coast.

iceland/solheimajokull-glacier-walk.name: Sólheimajökull glacier walk
iceland/solheimajokull-glacier-walk.description: A guided walk on the ice of an outlet glacier of Mýrdalsjökull, with crampons and an ice axe.
iceland/solheimajokull-glacier-walk.details: Sólheimajökull is an outlet glacier near the Ring Road that retreats noticeably year by year. Guided walks provide crampons, ice axes and helmets and lead small groups across the ice, past crevasses and meltwater channels. The walks are easy but need reasonable fitness and sturdy hiking boots. Tours depend on conditions and are cancelled in poor weather.

iceland/skaftafell-svartifoss.name: Skaftafell and Svartifoss
iceland/skaftafell-svartifoss.description: A walk in Vatnajökull National Park to a waterfall framed by hexagonal basalt columns.
iceland/skaftafell-svartifoss.details: Skaftafell is part of Vatnajökull National Park and has marked trails through birch scrub and heath beneath glaciers. The most popular is the walk of about an hour and a half return to Svartifoss, a waterfall that drops over a curved wall of dark basalt columns. The path climbs steadily and can be icy in winter. The visitor centre has maps and information about conditions.

iceland/skaftafell-glacier-hike.name: Glacier hike at Skaftafell
iceland/skaftafell-glacier-hike.description: A guided walk on a tongue of Vatnajökull, Europe's largest ice cap by volume.
iceland/skaftafell-glacier-hike.details: Guided glacier hikes in the Skaftafell area take small groups onto an outlet glacier of Vatnajökull, wearing crampons and carrying ice axes. The ice is full of crevasses, blue ice and meltwater streams, and guides explain how the glacier changes. Tours last around three to four hours and need good boots and fitness. They are cancelled in bad weather, so allow a spare day if you can.

iceland/jokulsarlon.name: Jökulsárlón glacier lagoon
iceland/jokulsarlon.description: A lagoon filled with floating icebergs calved from the Breiðamerkurjökull glacier, draining to the sea.
iceland/jokulsarlon.details: Jökulsárlón is a deep lagoon where icebergs break from the glacier edge and drift slowly toward a narrow channel to the Atlantic. Seals often rest on the ice, and the icebergs vary from white to deep blue. Boat tours across the lagoon run mainly in the warmer months. The stretch of shore is popular, so it is busy at midday and quietest in the early morning and evening.

iceland/diamond-beach.name: Diamond Beach
iceland/diamond-beach.description: A black sand beach across the road from Jökulsárlón, scattered with chunks of ice washed up by the surf.
iceland/diamond-beach.details: Diamond Beach lies where the channel from Jökulsárlón meets the sea, and pieces of ice from the lagoon wash up on the black sand, glittering as they melt. It is best at sunrise or sunset when the light catches the ice. The sea here is dangerous with strong currents and large waves, so keep well back from the water and never climb onto the ice. The beach is free to visit.

iceland/hofn-langoustine.name: Langoustine dinner in Höfn
iceland/hofn-langoustine.description: A meal of Icelandic langoustine, the small lobster for which the fishing town of Höfn is known.
iceland/hofn-langoustine.details: Höfn is a harbour town on the south-east coast with a reputation for langoustine, sometimes called Icelandic lobster, caught offshore and served grilled, in soup or on pasta. Several restaurants near the harbour specialise in it. The town is small and kitchens may close earlier than in Reykjavik, particularly outside summer, so book or arrive by seven. A langoustine festival is held in summer.

iceland/vestrahorn.name: Vestrahorn and Stokksnes
iceland/vestrahorn.description: A jagged mountain rising behind black sand dunes and a shallow bay on a peninsula near Höfn.
iceland/vestrahorn.details: Vestrahorn is a dramatic mountain of dark gabbro on the Stokksnes peninsula, rising above rippling black sand dunes and a tidal beach. It is one of the most photographed views in the south-east, particularly at low tide when the wet sand reflects the peak. The land is private and a small access fee is charged at the entrance. The wind is often strong and carries sand.

iceland/east-fjords-drive.name: East Fjords coastal drive
iceland/east-fjords-drive.description: A scenic drive along the road that winds in and out of the steep fjords of eastern Iceland.
iceland/east-fjords-drive.details: Between Höfn and Egilsstaðir, the road follows the east coast, running along fjord shores and crossing headlands past small fishing villages such as Djúpivogur. Mountains rise steeply from the water and there are few other cars. The drive is long, and fuel and services are sparse, so fill the tank when you can. Fog and wind can reduce visibility and winter conditions can close the mountain passes.

iceland/seydisfjordur.name: Seyðisfjörður
iceland/seydisfjordur.description: A small town at the head of a long fjord, with brightly coloured wooden houses and a church at the end of a rainbow-painted street.
iceland/seydisfjordur.details: Seyðisfjörður sits at the end of a narrow fjord reached by a mountain road over the Fjarðarheiði pass, which is often snowy and sometimes closed in winter. The town has well-preserved timber houses, a blue church at the end of a rainbow-painted street, a lively arts community and waterfalls on the slopes above it. It is also the port for the car ferry from Denmark. It is a quiet, atmospheric spot with a few cafes.

iceland/hengifoss.name: Hengifoss
iceland/hengifoss.description: A tall waterfall in the east with red clay bands in the rock behind it, reached by a steep walk.
iceland/hengifoss.details: Hengifoss drops some 128 metres, one of the highest waterfalls in the country, over cliffs with distinct red layers of clay between dark basalt. The trail from the car park climbs steadily for about two and a half kilometres, passing the smaller Litlanesfoss, which is framed by basalt columns. It takes around two and a half hours return and can be wet and slippery. It lies near Lagarfljót lake, not far from Egilsstaðir.

iceland/dettifoss.name: Dettifoss
iceland/dettifoss.description: The most powerful waterfall in Europe by volume, thundering into a canyon in the north-east.
iceland/dettifoss.details: Dettifoss is a hundred metres wide and drops forty-four metres into the Jökulsárgljúfur canyon, with a thunderous roar and clouds of spray. It can be reached from the western side by a paved road, or the eastern side by a gravel road, which has a better view but is rougher. Both roads are closed in winter. Paths near the falls are slippery, and there are steep drops with few barriers.

iceland/hverir-geothermal.name: Hverir geothermal area
iceland/hverir-geothermal.description: A barren field of bubbling mud pots and steaming vents on the way to Mývatn, smelling strongly of sulphur.
iceland/hverir-geothermal.details: Hverir, also called Námaskarð, is a geothermal field of orange, yellow and grey ground with boiling mud pots and hissing fumaroles. The sulphur smell is strong and the ground is dangerously hot, so keep to the marked paths and barriers. It is a short stop near the Ring Road, and very striking in low light. The surface is soft in places.

iceland/myvatn-lava-craters.name: Dimmuborgir and the Mývatn craters
iceland/myvatn-lava-craters.description: A field of twisted lava formations and rows of small pseudocraters beside the shallow lake of Mývatn.
iceland/myvatn-lava-craters.details: Lake Mývatn lies in a volcanic area and is surrounded by unusual landforms, including Dimmuborgir, a maze of lava pillars and arches whose name means dark castles, and the pseudocraters at Skútustaðir, formed by gas explosions in cooling lava. Marked trails lead through both. In summer, swarms of midges are a nuisance around the lake, and a head net helps. Birdlife on the lake is rich.

iceland/myvatn-nature-baths.name: Mývatn Nature Baths
iceland/myvatn-nature-baths.description: A geothermal lagoon in the north with milky blue water, less crowded than its southern counterpart.
iceland/myvatn-nature-baths.details: The Mývatn Nature Baths are filled with warm mineral water from a nearby borehole and have views over the lava landscape. It is smaller and generally quieter than the Blue Lagoon. Entry is by timed ticket, which is worth booking ahead in the high season. Showers before entering are required, and the evening is a good time to go after a day of driving.

iceland/godafoss.name: Goðafoss
iceland/godafoss.description: The Waterfall of the Gods, a horseshoe-shaped fall on the Skjálfandafljót river, linked to Iceland's conversion to Christianity.
iceland/godafoss.details: Goðafoss is a wide, curved waterfall around twelve metres high, easy to reach from a car park next to the Ring Road. It takes its name from the story that, when Iceland adopted Christianity around the year 1000, a chieftain threw statues of the old gods into the falls. Paths lead to viewpoints on both banks. The paths can be icy in winter.

iceland/husavik-whale-watching.name: Whale-watching from Húsavík
iceland/husavik-whale-watching.description: A boat trip from the small northern town of Húsavík, where humpback whales are seen on most summer trips.
iceland/husavik-whale-watching.details: Húsavík lies on Skjálfandi bay and is regarded as Iceland's whale-watching capital, with high success rates for humpbacks, minkes and dolphins on summer trips. Some tours use restored wooden fishing boats, and warm overalls are provided. Trips last about three hours, and the town has a whale museum. Cold winds are common even in summer, so wear layers.

iceland/akureyri.name: Akureyri
iceland/akureyri.description: Iceland's northern capital at the head of a long fjord, with a hilltop church, a botanical garden and a relaxed cafe scene.
iceland/akureyri.details: Akureyri is the second-largest urban area outside the Reykjavik region and sits beneath snow-capped mountains at the end of the Eyjafjörður fjord. The Akureyrarkirkja church, designed by the same architect as Hallgrímskirkja, overlooks the town from a hill. The botanical garden is among the world's northernmost, and traffic lights in the town centre are shaped like hearts. It is a pleasant town for walking, cafes and the surrounding scenery.

iceland/kirkjufell.name: Kirkjufell
iceland/kirkjufell.description: A cone-shaped mountain on the Snæfellsnes peninsula that is among the most photographed in Iceland, beside a small waterfall.
iceland/kirkjufell.details: Kirkjufell, whose name means church mountain, is a 463-metre peak that rises steeply from the shore near Grundarfjörður, with Kirkjufellsfoss, a small waterfall, in the foreground. It is much photographed, particularly in the evening and under the northern lights in winter. The viewing area is easily accessible from the road. The climb to the summit is steep and dangerous and not recommended.

iceland/arnarstapi-hellnar.name: Arnarstapi to Hellnar coastal walk
iceland/arnarstapi-hellnar.description: A path of a few kilometres along basalt cliffs and lava between two small fishing villages on the Snæfellsnes coast.
iceland/arnarstapi-hellnar.details: A well-marked path runs for around two and a half kilometres between the tiny villages of Arnarstapi and Hellnar, along sea cliffs of basalt columns, arches and lava formations, with large colonies of nesting seabirds in summer. It is mostly flat and takes about an hour each way. Wind and spray can be strong, so waterproofs help. Both villages have a cafe.

iceland/djupalonssandur.name: Djúpalónssandur
iceland/djupalonssandur.description: A black pebble beach strewn with rusted remains of a shipwreck and old stones once used to test fishermen's strength.
iceland/djupalonssandur.details: Djúpalónssandur lies at the foot of the Snæfellsjökull glacier, reached by a short path through a lava gap. The beach has smooth black pebbles, the rusting remains of a trawler wrecked in 1948, and four lifting stones used to test the strength of fishermen hoping to be hired. Waves are strong and dangerous, so keep away from the water. Taking pebbles is discouraged to protect the site.

iceland/stykkisholmur.name: Stykkishólmur
iceland/stykkisholmur.description: A harbour town on the Snæfellsnes peninsula with colourful old wooden houses, a lighthouse hill and views over Breiðafjörður.
iceland/stykkisholmur.details: Stykkishólmur is one of the prettiest towns in the west, with painted wooden houses, a working harbour and a small island viewpoint, Súgandisey, reached by a short climb. It is also the port for the ferry across Breiðafjörður to the Westfjords. The Norwegian House museum shows life in the nineteenth century. It is a relaxed place for a night after the long drive from the north.

iceland/hraunfossar.name: Hraunfossar and Barnafoss
iceland/hraunfossar.description: Waterfalls that seep out of the edge of a lava field and pour into the Hvítá river in west Iceland.
iceland/hraunfossar.details: Hraunfossar are an unusual series of waterfalls that emerge from under the edge of an old lava field and flow into the Hvítá river over a distance of several hundred metres. Barnafoss, a short walk upriver, is a narrow cascade through a rocky channel. The area is easily reached by boardwalk and viewing platforms. Nearby, Deildartunguhver is the highest-flow hot spring in Europe, which makes a good stop on the way.

iceland.name: Iceland
iceland.description: An island of waterfalls, glaciers, black sand beaches and geothermal pools, best seen on a self-drive loop.

iceland/capital-region.name: Capital Region
iceland/capital-region.description: The area around Reykjavik, which holds about two-thirds of the country's people and the international airport nearby.

iceland/reykjavik.name: Reykjavik
iceland/reykjavik.description: The world's northernmost capital, a small colourful city of cafes, museums and a harbour, and the base for day trips.

iceland/south-iceland.name: South Iceland
iceland/south-iceland.description: The region of the Golden Circle and the south coast, with waterfalls, black beaches and glacier tongues.

iceland/golden-circle.name: Golden Circle
iceland/golden-circle.description: A loop east of Reykjavik linking Thingvellir National Park, the Geysir geothermal area and Gullfoss waterfall.

iceland/vik.name: Vik
iceland/vik.description: The southernmost village in Iceland, beside the black sand beach of Reynisfjara and a base for the south coast.

iceland/skaftafell.name: Skaftafell
iceland/skaftafell.description: A part of Vatnajökull National Park with hiking trails, the Svartifoss waterfall and guided glacier walks.

iceland/jokulsarlon.name: Jokulsarlon
iceland/jokulsarlon.description: A glacier lagoon of floating icebergs on the south-east coast, beside the ice-strewn Diamond Beach.

iceland/hofn.name: Hofn
iceland/hofn.description: A harbour town in the south-east known for langoustine and views of the Vatnajökull glacier.

iceland/east-iceland.name: East Iceland
iceland/east-iceland.description: A quiet region of fjords, small fishing villages and mountains, with the town of Egilsstaðir at its centre.

iceland/egilsstadir.name: Egilsstadir
iceland/egilsstadir.description: The largest town in the east, beside Lagarfljót lake, and a base for the Hengifoss waterfall and Seyðisfjörður.

iceland/seydisfjordur.name: Seydisfjordur
iceland/seydisfjordur.description: A small arts town at the head of a long fjord, with a rainbow street and a ferry link to Denmark.

iceland/north-iceland.name: North Iceland
iceland/north-iceland.description: The region of Akureyri, Lake Mývatn, waterfalls and whale watching, with a wild, volcanic landscape.

iceland/myvatn.name: Myvatn
iceland/myvatn.description: A shallow volcanic lake in the north surrounded by lava fields, craters, mud pots and geothermal baths.

iceland/akureyri.name: Akureyri
iceland/akureyri.description: Iceland's northern capital at the head of the Eyjafjörður fjord, with a botanical garden and a hilltop church.

iceland/husavik.name: Husavik
iceland/husavik.description: A small town on Skjálfandi bay that is the whale-watching capital of Iceland.

iceland/west-iceland.name: West Iceland
iceland/west-iceland.description: A region of lava fields, waterfalls and the Snæfellsnes peninsula, within a few hours of Reykjavik.

iceland/snaefellsnes.name: Snaefellsnes
iceland/snaefellsnes.description: A peninsula in the west sometimes called Iceland in miniature, with a glacier-capped volcano, black beaches and a photogenic mountain.

iceland/stykkisholmur.name: Stykkisholmur
iceland/stykkisholmur.description: A pretty harbour town on Snæfellsnes with painted wooden houses and a ferry to the Westfjords.

iceland/borgarnes.name: Borgarnes
iceland/borgarnes.description: A small town on a fjord north of Reykjavik, handy as a stop and a base for the Hraunfossar waterfalls.
